questions.q: Why does this report need to be published to the Power BI Service rather than just left in Power BI Desktop?
options: The Merchandising Manager doesn't have Power BI Desktop open and shouldn't need it -- the Service is where a finished report is actually handed to a stakeholder
DAX measures only calculate correctly after publishing
Power BI Desktop cannot save a .pbix file with a native query in it
Publishing is required before a slicer can be added to a report
questions.explain: Desktop is the build tool; the Service is where someone without Desktop installed can actually open and use the report.

questions.q: Why is My Workspace the wrong destination for this report's final publish?
options: My Workspace isn't shareable with anyone else, so it can't be used to deliver the report to the Merchandising Manager
My Workspace does not support DAX measures
My Workspace has a four-report limit
My Workspace requires a separate Power BI license to use
questions.explain: My Workspace is for personal testing; a shared workspace is needed so the report can actually be shared with the stakeholder.

questions.q: What are the two separate objects Power BI uploads when you publish this report?
options: The dataset (the model, table, and measures) and the report (the pages and visuals)
The .pbix file and a .csv export of the data
The slicer settings and the color theme
The T-SQL query and the Power Query transformations
questions.explain: Even though they come from one .pbix file, the Service lists the dataset and the report as two related but separate objects in the workspace.

questions.q: If the AdventureWorks2012 data needs a refresh next quarter, whose settings matter?
options: The dataset's refresh settings
The report's refresh settings
The slicer's refresh settings
There is no refresh setting in the Power BI Service
questions.explain: The dataset holds the actual data model; refresh schedules are configured there, not on the report object.

questions.q: Why is a direct share -- not a full Power BI App -- the right way to deliver this report?
options: This is a single named stakeholder with no existing company-wide dashboard; a full App makes sense once multiple reports and audiences exist
Power BI Apps cannot contain reports built from a native query
Direct sharing is required whenever a slicer is used
A Power BI App always costs an additional license per viewer
questions.explain: A packaged App is the right structure for multiple reports and audiences; for one stakeholder and one report, direct sharing matches the actual scope.
